newsitem.title: UK: LME to declare options automatically in June.
newsitem.headline: LME to declare options automatically in June.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) is to adopt a procedure where certain Exchange options will be automatically declared if they are in-the-money.
In a notice to members the LME said this will be implemented for the June 1997 declarations.

It will apply to traded options for copper, aluminium, tin, lead, zinc, nickel and aluminium alloy. The LME's new cash-settled traded average price options (TAPO) in copper and aluminium are already automatically declared.

The LME said that at 1700 hours on the last trading day before expiry (usually the Tuesday prior to declaration on the first Wednesday of the month) the Exchange Executive will calculate the at-the-money strike price and the range of options that will be automatically declared.
The at-the-money price will be the strike price that is closest to the relevant prompt date futures price. Two gradations (strikes) will also be identified above and below the at-the-money strike.
Calls that are two or more gradations below the at-the-money strike will be automatically declared. Puts two or more gradations above will similarly be automatically declared.
All other Exchange options will be subject to manual declaration. If there is excessive overnight price movement the automatic exercise can be manually reversed.
LME Chief Executive David King said the objective of this was to remove the possibility of errors arising in declaration.
"It brings us into line with the procedure in other markets," he said.
Miles Linington, Chairman of the LME's traded options subcommittee, noted that option traders retained flexibility during declaration if there were sharp price moves.
"This is all part of moving forward and using technology," he added.
